extracted.intended_audience: TV industry observers, media analysts, and general readers interested in streaming/television trends
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and reporting of metrics used to measure and compare TV series cancellation behavior across streaming and linear platforms (2020–Aug. 8, 2023). Includes platform-level cancellation rates, breakdowns by genre/format/season length, ownership status, and time trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform cancellation rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Average cancellation rate for a given platform (e.g., Max 26.9%, Netflix 10.2%, Apple TV+ 4.9%) measured over 2020 through Aug. 8, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare how often each streamer or linear outlet cancels series; the article reports platform-level percentages and rankings (Max most, Apple least). Interpret in context with other metrics such as volume of output and ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yearly cancellation rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Cancellation rates calculated separately for each year (2020, 2021, 2022, 2023 to date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows analysis of trends over time (e.g., rates dropped consecutively from 2020 through 2023 across streaming, linear, and overall series-TV).

rubrics_metrics.name: Total seasons released
rubrics_metrics.description: Total count of seasons released by a platform/group during the measurement period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides scale of output and contextualizes cancellation counts and rates (more seasons released can affect perceived cancellation frequency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Total unique series
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of unique series released by a platform/group in the measurement window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compute cancellation rates and to compare content volume across services (Netflix's large volume contributes to its reputation for cancellations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross series cancellations
rubrics_metrics.description: Total number of series cancellations (raw count) on a platform/group during the period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raw cancellation counts complement rates; e.g., 221 cancellations across major streamers vs. 193 on linear TV from 2020–2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited series output
rubrics_metrics.description: Number or share of limited (designed-to-end) series produced by a platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes between planned limited runs and continuing series, which affects how many cancellations are expected or counted as 'cancels.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of limited series vs. continuing series
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of a platform's output that is limited-series compared to continuing series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps separate planned endings from true cancellations; platforms with many limited series will naturally show different cancellation dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total planned endings
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of series that concluded as planned (not canceled) in the measurement period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare against canceled shows to understand what portion of series endings were intentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of planned endings vs. canceled
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of series endings that were planned finales versus cancellations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides perspective on whether high ‘ending’ numbers reflect creative choice or cancellations; important when interpreting platform behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scripted vs. unscripted unique series released
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate counts (or shares) of scripted and unscripted unique series produced/released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows disaggregation of cancellation patterns by format; platforms may behave differently toward scripted vs. unscripted fare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation rates of scripted vs. unscripted
rubrics_metrics.description: Rates at which scripted shows are canceled versus unscripted shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative metric to see if one format is more likely to be canceled; article notes streaming scripted vs. unscripted distinctions are tracked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of canceled shows across comedy, drama, animation, unscripted
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown of canceled shows by genre/category (comedy, drama, animation, unscripted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reveals genre-specific cancellation patterns and whether certain genres are more vulnerable to cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average number of seasons before cancellations
rubrics_metrics.description: Mean number of seasons a show runs before being canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates platform patience; the report finds streaming platforms tended to cancel earlier (more first-season cancellations) while broadcast/cable were slightly more patient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of cancellations by length of series (1 to 6+ seasons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of canceled series by how many seasons they had (e.g., share canceled after season 1, 2, ... 6+).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for understanding whether cancellations are concentrated among very new shows or spread across longer-running series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of unique original series owned vs. not owned
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of unique original series on a platform that are owned by the platform vs. not owned (licensed or third-party).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership status can affect cancellation decisions and accounting; tracked to compare behavior toward owned vs. non-owned originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancel rates: original series owned vs. not owned
rubrics_metrics.description: Cancellation rates for original series that are owned by the platform versus those that are not owned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables analysis of whether platforms are more likely to cancel shows they own or shows they license; ownership can influence renewal economics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gross cancels: original series owned vs. not owned
rubrics_metrics.description: Raw counts of cancellations split by ownership status (owned originals vs. non-owned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complements rate-based comparisons with absolute numbers to see which categories contribute most to cancellations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset inclusion window
rubrics_metrics.description: The study covers all shows canceled between 2020 and Aug. 8, 2023 (scripted and unscripted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the temporal scope of the analysis; results and trends apply to this timeframe and may be influenced by events in those years (e.g., strikes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform grouping and comparisons (streaming, linear, broadcast, cable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grouping cancellations by distribution type — aggregate streaming, broadcast, cable, linear TV — to compare across business models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to highlight differences (or lack thereof) in cancellation behavior across distribution types; the report notes combined streaming avg 12.2% vs. linear 10.8% and broadcast higher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume-of-output caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Caveat that the absolute volume of shows produced/released varies widely across platforms and influences perceptions of cancellation behavior (e.g., Netflix's large volume draws criticism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises interpreting cancellation rates in context of output volume; a low rate on a high-volume platform can still mean a large absolute number of cancellations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trend analysis (improvement or worsening over time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tracking whether cancellation rates worsen or improve over the years (e.g., Netflix improved its cancellation rate every year from 2020–2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important for addressing perceptions about whether cancellations are increasing industry-wide; the study finds rates dropped across the board during the period analyzed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tendency to cancel first-season shows
rubrics_metrics.description: Metric/observation that platforms tended to mostly cancel first-season shows rather than longer-running series, with streaming slightly more likely to pull the plug earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights that cancellations are concentrated among new shows; use season-by-season breakdowns to evaluate platform patience.
